label: benign
description: Professional typesetting that uses format characters for their intended purpose: soft hyphens at genuine syllable breaks in long words, word joiners preventing breaks, no-break and thin spaces, curly quotes, dashes, ellipsis, and a leading byte order mark on exported files. The attack corpus reuses these codepoints to split short keywords; the length, position, and context here are what make each use legitimate.

cases.title: Typeset novel paragraph with curly quotes and em dashes
cases.text: ‘You said the letters would come by Friday,’ she said — not accusingly, but close to it. The room went quiet the way rooms do when everyone is counting someone else’s breaths. Outside, the harbour lights came on, one by one, until the dark simply gave up…
cases.rationale: A typeset fiction paragraph whose non-ASCII characters are ordinary professional punctuation — curly single quotes, em dashes, apostrophe, and ellipsis — visible in any printed book.

cases.title: German compound with soft hyphens at morpheme breaks
cases.text: Die Donau­dampf­schiff­fahrts­gesellschaft nahm 1889 ihren regelmässigen Betrieb auf. Bei einer Länge von 39 Buchstaben braucht das Wort an jeder Fuge einen Trennstrich-Vorschlag.
cases.rationale: The soft hyphens sit only at the morpheme boundaries of a 39-letter German compound (Donau·dampf·schiff·fahrts·gesellschaft), the exact legitimate use of U+00AD that a narrow column needs to typeset it.

cases.title: CSV export opening with a byte order mark
cases.text:
﻿order_id,placed_at,item,quantity,total
50931,2025-06-02,Spring washers M8,400,18.60
50932,2025-06-02,Hex bolts M8 x 40,250,22.15
50933,2025-06-03,Nylon spacers 6 mm,1200,41.02
cases.rationale: The leading U+FEFF is the byte order mark that spreadsheet exports prepend so Excel detects UTF-8; it is a file signature here, not hidden text, and the rest is an ordinary order extract.

cases.title: Price list with no-break and narrow no-break spaces
cases.text:
Preisliste, Stand 3. März

Kaffeebohnen, 1 kg — 17,90 €
Olivenöl, 0,7 l — 11,40 €
Rührei-Ersatz, 6 × 500 g — 2 450,00 €
Alle Preise inkl. MwSt; Irrtümer vorbehalten.
cases.rationale: The no-break space, thin space, and narrow no-break space keep each amount and its unit on one line, which is precisely what no-break spaces exist for in a price list.

cases.title: Dictionary publisher note on hyphenation points
cases.text: House style: break in­ter­na­tion­al­iza­tion only at the dictionary's marked points, and treat pro­gram­mat­ical­ly the same way. Never hyphenate a headword shorter than six letters.
cases.rationale: The soft hyphens mark genuine syllable boundaries (in·ter·na·tion·al·iza·tion) in words many letters long, not splits planted inside a short keyword as the attack family does.

cases.title: Standard designations bound with word joiners
cases.text: All gaskets conform to ISO⁠/⁠IEC⁠/⁠DIN⁠/⁠EN 22857 and to the flange classes in ASME⁠/⁠ANSI B16.5; substitutions require sign⁠/⁠off from the chief engineer.
cases.rationale: The word joiner forbids a line break at each slash so a standard's designation can never be split across lines, its textbook legitimate use.

cases.title: French paragraph with required no-break spaces
cases.text: Bonjour ! Le train part à 7 h 30 ; sois à la gare 20 minutes avant. Apporte : les billets, une pièce d'identité, et un parapluie !
cases.rationale: French typography requires a no-break space before ! : ; ? and inside time expressions, so every U+00A0 here is a rule of the language, not a hidden separator.

cases.title: Editorial paragraph using en and em dashes
cases.text: The collected letters, covering 1914–18 and running to 912–980 pages in draft, arrive in January. They are lively — occasionally spiteful — and the index alone took a year; the maps (pages 44–52, 61–63) were redrawn twice.
cases.rationale: The en dashes carry numeric ranges and the em dashes an aside, which is the standard distinction professional copy-editors make between the two dashes.

cases.title: Specification sheet with thin-space digit grouping
cases.text: Rotor diameter 10 400 mm; mass 1 268 kg; rated speed 1 490 rpm; air gap flux 0,96 T. Dimensions are measured at 20 °C ± 0,5 °C per the works standard.
cases.rationale: Thin spaces group digits in engineering numbers without permitting a line break inside a value, and the surrounding text is an ordinary specification sheet.

cases.title: Recipe with curly apostrophes and en dash timing
cases.text: Don’t overwork the batter — fold just until the flour disappears. Rest 10–12 minutes while the pan returns to medium heat, then ladle, tilt, and wait for the edges to set; the second crêpe always beats the first.
cases.rationale: A home-cooking paragraph whose only non-ASCII characters are a curly apostrophe, an em dash, and en dashes in a timing range, all fully visible.

cases.title: Narrow-column news item hyphenating a long medical term
cases.text: The clinic's pilot programme screens for pseu­do­hy­po­par­a­thy­roid­ism, and in a three-column layout even the shorter thy­roid­ecto­my must break somewhere; editors follow the dictionary, which splits only at syllables.
cases.rationale: The soft hyphens fall at the syllable boundaries a dictionary specifies for a thirteen-syllable medical word in a narrow column, a legitimate use of U+00AD that never touches a short keyword.

cases.title: JSONL export carrying a byte order mark
cases.rationale: The export pipeline writes a U+FEFF signature so downstream Windows tools detect UTF-8, and the rows are ordinary accounting records with visible accented names.
